verdict.rationale: Gram supports RBAC/OAuth2.1 permissions enforced at team, server, and tool level synced to enterprise IDPs, and MoonPay's case study shows permissions 'scoped per server, per tool, and per team' via Okta — this is credential/permission scoping, though framed at the team/role level rather than per-agent-instance issuance. External OAuth provider support for MCP servers also exists. However, there's no explicit documentation of issuing narrowly-scoped, short-lived, or dynamically-provisioned credentials specifically to an individual autonomous agent (vs. a human user/team role), nor evidence of fine-grained least-privilege token minting per agent session. Missing for 10: explicit per-agent (not just per-team/role) credential issuance workflow, evidence of scoped/short-lived token generation for individual agent sessions, and independent/hands-on verification of least-privilege enforcement.
